summary.headline: The Egyptian Astrologer of 379
summary.text: Editorial discussion of an Egyptian astrologer active in Rome in 379 A.D., whose chapters on stars rising with the zodiac signs and astrological doctrine draw heavily on Ptolemy’s Tetrabiblos and Egyptian religious lore. The editor identifies three related chapters preserved by Palchus, notes their astronomical computations and possible links to Codex Venet. 7, and cautiously considers Paulus Alexandrinus as the unnamed author.
